findings.title: Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is started.
findings.body: `self.mp_context.Process` builds a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` inherits from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (the default context's `Process` class), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False here. The old code called `self.process.kill()` with no condition. Now a process that hangs (no progress for `max-unhealthy-seconds`) keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new one for the same shards. Two flushers then work on the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate segments, and a leaked process piles up on every restart. Fix: check for `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead, or check `hasattr(process, "kill")`, so threads used in tests are still skipped.

findings.title: join() stops before terminating the remaining processes once the deadline passes.
findings.body: When the deadline runs out while join() is waiting on one process, the next loop iteration hits `break` before reaching `terminate()`. Every later process is left running, even if it is hung. The old code always terminated its process after the wait. The same faulty `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check also means `terminate()` is never actually called for spawned processes. Fix: wait while time remains, but always run the terminate step for every process (check for `BaseProcess` or use `hasattr(process, "terminate")`), even after the deadline.

findings.title: The wait_produce metric uses the tag key `shards`, while sibling metrics use `shard`.
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged `shard`, but `wait_produce` is tagged `shards`. Dashboards that filter or group these metrics by one key will miss this one. Use the same tag key everywhere.
